translationRepairs: The Founder Emperor rose from commoner rank, knew the hardship of the people's affairs; when he ascended the throne and became chief minister, he paid attention to officials' duties, but royal strategy looked outward and he had no leisure for internal administration.

The Founder Emperor rose from commoner rank, knew the hardship of the people's affairs; when he was raised to serve as chief minister, he paid attention to officials' duties, but royal strategy looked outward and he had no leisure for internal administration.

登庸作宰 is elevation to the chief-ministership, not accession; 高祖 here is still the Jin power-holder, and the throne is a later event (踐阼). Replacing 'ascended the throne and became chief minister' removes an invented coronation.
Wang Yu's son Sui was Huan Xuan's nephew by marriage and immensely powerful at court. Zhenzhi was forced out and, pleading his mother's advanced age, asked to be appointed administrator of Ancheng.
Wang Yu's son Sui was Huan Xuan's sister's son and immensely powerful at court. Zhenzhi was forced out and, pleading his mother's advanced age, asked to be appointed administrator of Ancheng.
外甥 is a sister's son (maternal nephew). 'Nephew by marriage' invents an affinal tie the Chinese does not state.
When mourning was over, he became Marshal of the Western Expeditionary Army under Dao Gui and Administrator of Nanping.
When mourning was over, he became Marshal of the Western Expeditionary Army under Daogui and Administrator of Nanping.
道規 is the undivided personal name Daogui (Liu Daogui). Splitting it as 'Dao Gui' treats one name as two syllables and is a naming error, not a style choice.
He was appointed General of Agile Cavalry.
除龍驤將軍 is Dragon-soaring General. General of Agile Cavalry renders 驍騎, a different title.
Yuan was then appointed General of Agile Cavalry and inspector of Jiaozhou.
Yuan was then appointed Dragon-soaring General and inspector of Jiaozhou.
乃以瑗為龍驤將軍 repeats the same title as s0056; 'General of Agile Cavalry' is again 驍騎, not 龍驤.
When Liu Yu raised the banner of righteous restoration, Yuan was promoted to General Who Conquers.
When Liu Yu raised the banner of righteous restoration, Yuan was promoted to Champion General.
冠軍將軍 is Champion General. 'General Who Conquers' invents a different honorific (as if 征 or 平).
When the Banner of Righteousness rose, his title was advanced to General Who Conquers.
When the Banner of Righteousness rose, his title was advanced to Champion General.
The literal likewise misrenders 冠軍將軍 as 'General Who Conquers'; Champion General is the correct title.
They beheaded Lu Xun, his father Gu, and his two sons, along with his kinsmen Sun Jing, Luo Nongfu, Li Tuo, and others, and sent their heads to the capital.
They beheaded Lu Xun, his father Gu, and his two sons, along with his kinsmen Ruan Jing, Luo Nongfu, Li Tuo, and others, and sent their heads to the capital.
親屬錄事參軍阮靜 names Ruan Jing. Sun Jing has no source in 阮 and is a surname error.
They beheaded Xun and his father Gu, together with Xun's two sons, and kinsmen Recorder Sun Jing, Central Army Adjutant Luo Nongfu, Li Tuo, and others; their heads were sent to the capital.
They beheaded Xun and his father Gu, together with Xun's two sons, and kinsmen Recorder Ruan Jing, Central Army Adjutant Luo Nongfu, Li Tuo, and others; their heads were sent to the capital.
The literal repeats the same false surname for 阮靜; Ruan Jing restores the Chinese name.
Huidu's eldest son Hongwen, an attendant gentleman at the Secretariat, was appointed General Who Quells Might and inspector of Jiaozhou.
Huidu's eldest son Hongwen, Attendant Gentleman at the Secretariat Outside the Palace, was appointed General Who Quells Might and inspector of Jiaozhou.

員外散騎侍郎 was dropped, which is a real omission, but stripping Jiaozhou from 刺史 leaves an incomplete idiomatic office: after Huidu's death the ungoverned 刺史 is his Jiaozhou inspectorship. Restore 員外 and keep Jiaozhou.
Xu Huo, courtesy name Wantong, was from Gumu in Dongguan and nephew of Palace Attendant Xu Guang.
Xu Huo, courtesy name Wantong, was from Gumu in Dongguan and nephew of Grand Master of Palace Leisure Xu Guang.
中散大夫 is Grand Master of Palace Leisure, not Palace Attendant (侍中).
Xu Huo, styled Wantong, was a man of Gumu in Dongguan, nephew of Palace Attendant Xu Guang.
Xu Huo, styled Wantong, was a man of Gumu in Dongguan, nephew of Grand Master of Palace Leisure Xu Guang.
The literal makes the same 中散大夫 / 侍中 substitution; Grand Master of Palace Leisure matches the Chinese office.

When Huan Xuan held power as area commander of inner and outer affairs, Huo argued: "Bowing in respect applies only to military officials. The Grand Tutor and Minister over the Masses are not military posts, so the Prince of Langye should not receive added obeisance."

When Huan Xuan held power as area commander of inner and outer affairs, Huo argued: "Bowing in respect applies only to inner and outer military officials. The Grand Steward and Minister over the Masses are not military posts, so the Prince of Langye should not receive added obeisance."
太宰 is Grand Steward, not Grand Tutor (太傅), and 致敬唯內外武官 specifies inner and outer military officials. Both corrections are required by the Chinese.

When Huan Xuan assisted in government as Area Commander of Inner and Outer Affairs, Huo argued: "Bowing in respect is only for inner and outer military officials; the Grand Tutor and Minister over the Masses are not military posts, so the Prince of Langye should not be given added respect."

When Huan Xuan assisted in government as Area Commander of Inner and Outer Affairs, Huo argued: "Bowing in respect is only for inner and outer military officials; the Grand Steward and Minister over the Masses are not military posts, so the Prince of Langye should not be given added respect."
The literal already has inner and outer military officials but still mistranslates 太宰 as Grand Tutor; Grand Steward is the correct office.
At the beginning of Yongchu he served as marshal of the pacifying army under Xu Xianzhi, left assistant in the secretariat, and magistrate of Shanyin.
At the beginning of Yongchu he served as marshal of the garrison army under Xu Xianzhi, left assistant in the secretariat, and magistrate of Shanyin.
徐羨之鎮軍司馬 is staff marshal to Xu Xianzhi as Garrison (鎮軍) general, not a 'pacifying' (平) army.

In the fifth year he was made Bearer of the Staff, Commander over military affairs of Guang and Jiao provinces, General of Tranquil Distance, General Who Pacifies the Yue as Central Army Commander, and Inspector of Guangzhou.

In the fifth year he was made Bearer of the Staff, Commander over military affairs of Guang and Jiao provinces, General of Tranquil Distance, Commandant Who Pacifies the Yue, and Inspector of Guangzhou.

平越中郎將 is not 'Central Army Commander', so the original is wrong, but 'Household Gentleman General Who Pacifies the Yue' is still awkward. Use Commandant Who Pacifies the Yue, the same office restored in r0018.

The following year he was appointed bearer of the staff of authority, commander of Jiao and Guang military affairs, General of Pacifying Distance, General Who Pacifies the Yue, and inspector of Guangzhou.

The following year he was appointed bearer of the staff of authority, commander of Jiao and Guang military affairs, General of Pacifying Distance, Commandant Who Pacifies the Yue, and inspector of Guangzhou.
平越中郎將 is a distinct 中郎將 commandancy, not a generic 將軍. 'Commandant Who Pacifies the Yue' restores the dropped office type.
In the twenty-first year he was summoned to serve as marshal of the conquering army under Prince Shuo of Nanping, interior secretary of Changsha, and acting head of the Xiangzhou headquarters.
In the twenty-first year he was summoned to serve as marshal to the Champion General under Prince Shuo of Nanping, interior secretary of Changsha, and acting head of the Xiangzhou headquarters.
南平王鑠冠軍司馬 is marshal on the staff of the prince as Champion General (冠軍), not marshal of a 'conquering' army.
In the twenty-first year he was summoned as Marshal of the Conquering Army under the Prince of Nanping, Shuo, Interior Secretary of Changsha, acting in the affairs of the Xiangzhou headquarters.
In the twenty-first year he was summoned as Marshal to the Champion General under the Prince of Nanping, Shuo, Interior Secretary of Changsha, acting in the affairs of the Xiangzhou headquarters.
冠軍 must be Champion, not Conquering, but 'Champion Army' still invents an army name. The office is marshal to the Champion General.
He entered the secretariat as palace attendant and was then appointed administrator of Wuchang.
He entered the secretariat as gentleman of the palace section and was then appointed administrator of Wuchang.
尚書殿中郎 is a secretariat gentleman of the palace section, not Palace Attendant (侍中).
When Yin Jingren was area commander, he requested Bingzhi as his marshal.
When Yin Jingren was leader of the army, he requested Bingzhi as his marshal.
殷景仁為領軍 is Leader of the Army, not area commander (都督).
When Yin Jingren was Area Commander, he requested Bingzhi as Marshal.
When Yin Jingren was Leader of the Army, he requested Bingzhi as Marshal.
The literal makes the same 領軍 / 都督 substitution; Leader of the Army is the Chinese office.
When Prince Yuanxiong killed Xu Tanzhi, Hui was executed as his accomplice.
When Yuanxiong killed Xu Tanzhi, Hui was executed as his accomplice.
元兇 is the historiographical epithet for Liu Shao, not a princely title 'Prince Yuanxiong'. Dropping Prince removes the invented rank while keeping the established English for 元兇.
When the Prince of Yuanxiong killed Xu Tanzhi, Hui was executed as an associate.
When Yuanxiong killed Xu Tanzhi, Hui was executed as an associate.
The literal's 'Prince of Yuanxiong' likewise invents a fief-title from the epithet 元兇.
His son Mi served as gentleman of the personnel section at the end of the Shengping era.
His son Mi served as gentleman of the personnel section at the end of the Shengming era.
昇明 is the Shengming era (end of Song), not Shengping (升平).
His son Mi at the end of the Shengping era was Gentleman of the Personnel Section in the Secretariat.
His son Mi at the end of the Shengming era was Gentleman of the Personnel Section in the Secretariat.
The literal repeats the false era name Shengping for 昇明; Shengming is required.

In the ninth year of Yuanjia, Prince Yixin of Changsha, inspector of Yuzhou, reported: "General Who Establishes Distance Shen Jili, marquis within the passes and administrator of Bei, Qiao, and Liang, has served in the capital region for five years. His trustworthiness and kindness are felt throughout his districts; he has suppressed violence abroad and brought order at home; levies are fair and the people live in peace. He has pacified newly submitted peoples and drawn in the remote frontier. Beyond the suburbs the people look to his grace. His merit warrants promotion in rank as encouragement to others."

In the ninth year of Yuanjia, Prince Yixin of Changsha, inspector of Yuzhou, reported: "General Who Establishes Distance Shen Jili, marquis within the passes and administrator of Northern Qiao and Liang, has served in the capital region for five years. His trustworthiness and kindness are felt throughout his districts; he has suppressed violence abroad and brought order at home; levies are fair and the people live in peace. He has pacified newly submitted peoples and drawn in the remote frontier. Beyond the suburbs the people look to his grace. His merit warrants promotion in rank as encouragement to others."
北譙梁二郡 is two commanderies, Northern Qiao and Liang. Splitting 北譙 into Bei and Qiao invents a third place.

In the ninth year of Yuanjia the Inspector of Yuzhou, the Prince of Changsha Yixin, memorialized: "Under my command General Who Establishes Distance, Administrator of Bei and Qiao and Liang commanderies, Marquis within the Passes Shen Jili, since taking office in the capital region, for five years now, trust and kindness have both been proclaimed, authority and transformation both manifest; without he has cleared treachery and violence, within he has settled the people; corvée and levies are fair and even, lanes and wells are all orderly; he has pacified those newly attached and drawn in the remote and wild; beyond the suburbs they look up to his grace and cherish his wind; in granting titles and rewards, merit and ability are thereby displayed—he should be advanced in rank to honor and encourage."

In the ninth year of Yuanjia the Inspector of Yuzhou, the Prince of Changsha Yixin, memorialized: "Under my command General Who Establishes Distance, Administrator of Northern Qiao and Liang commanderies, Marquis within the Passes Shen Jili, since taking office in the capital region, for five years now, trust and kindness have both been proclaimed, authority and transformation both manifest; without he has cleared treachery and violence, within he has settled the people; corvée and levies are fair and even, lanes and wells are all orderly; he has pacified those newly attached and drawn in the remote and wild; beyond the suburbs they look up to his grace and cherish his wind; in granting titles and rewards, merit and ability are thereby displayed—he should be advanced in rank to honor and encourage."
The literal's 'Bei and Qiao and Liang commanderies' likewise splits 北譙 and ignores 二郡.

曾孫 is great-grandson, not great-great-grandson (玄孫). The Chinese identifies 羲之 by the Jin office 右將軍 and does not call him a calligrapher.
Yue, styled Shaoming, was a great-great-grandson of Xi Zhi, Right General of Jin.
Yue, styled Shaoming, was a great-grandson of Wang Xizhi, Right General of Jin.
The literal repeats the 曾孫 generation error and splits 羲之 as Xi Zhi; great-grandson of Wang Xizhi restores both the kinship and the name.
